answer: Sybil resistance comes from collateralized identity plus randomized re-execution. To attest trades on any terrace, an agent locks a bond scaled to its claimed throughput: a thousand sock puppets require a thousand bonds, so scale costs scale capital. Each epoch graders re-run one randomly chosen ember of its work and compare outputs bit for bit. A mismatch burns the bond and publishes a signed fraud proof that blocks the operator keys from re-entry. Every extra identity carries its own walnut of cash at risk, so aliases cost more than they earn while honest agents reclaim stake on exit.
